title: All things work together (Romans 8:28–30)
hook: for good, to those who love God

segments.voice: Yesterday, the groaning creation, and the Spirit praying in sighs too deep for words. Your line was the spirit prays with us. Did a breath or a hand on a shoulder do what words couldn't? Day three hundred twenty-two.

You've probably seen it on a mug, or a sympathy card, or heard it said at a funeral by someone trying to help: everything happens for a reason. Sometimes it lands gently. Sometimes it lands like a slap. Tell someone whose child is sick that it's all for a reason, and watch their face. The line people are often reaching for, whether they know it or not, is a single verse in Romans chapter eight. It's one of the most loved verses in the Bible and one of the most misquoted. So today, slowly: what does it actually say, and what doesn't it?
screen: `EVERYTHING HAPPENS FOR A REASON?` → `SOMETIMES A SLAP.` → `WHAT DOES THE VERSE ACTUALLY SAY?`

segments.voice: Here it is, in the King James Bible: "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose." First, what it doesn't say. It doesn't say all things are good. Paul has just spent a whole paragraph on suffering, groaning, a world in labor pains. He's not pretending cancer is good, or cruelty, or loss. Second, what it does say. Work together is one word in Greek, synergei. You can hear our word synergy in it. Things that are not good in themselves are worked together, woven, into something good. Picture a weaver using dark threads as well as bright ones, and the pattern only shows from the other side. And here's a detail worth knowing: some of the oldest manuscripts of Romans add two words, so the verse reads God works all things together for good. God is the weaver, not luck. Then verses twenty-nine and thirty trace a golden chain: those God foreknew, he predestined, called, justified and glorified. Christians read that chain differently. Reformed Christians, following Calvin, stress God's sovereign choice. Methodists and many others, following Wesley, stress that God's foreknowledge leaves room for human freedom. Catholic and Orthodox teaching holds God's grace and human cooperation together. All of them hear the same comfort: the story is held. This has been quite a week: peace with God, Adam and Christ, dead to sin, the wretched man, no condemnation, the groaning world. Today they all get woven together.
screen: `NOT: ALL THINGS ARE GOOD.` · `SYNERGEI: WOVEN TOGETHER.` · `GOD WORKS ALL THINGS TOGETHER.` · `A GOLDEN CHAIN, READ THREE WAYS.` · then, large: `ALL THINGS WORK TOGETHER FOR GOOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look for good inside a hard thing. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind something hard, maybe from this past week. Don't call it good. It may not be. Just look at it gently, the way you'd turn over a woven cloth to see the back. Is there one thread of good worked into it? A kindness someone showed you. Something you learned. A friend who showed up. If you can't find one yet, that's all right; Paul says we know, not that we always see. If you pray, you can hand the hard thing to God, the weaver. The bell holds the time.
All things work together. Synergei in Greek: not that all things are good, but that even hard things are woven into good.
Your line: all things work together. Today, if someone is hurting, skip everything happens for a reason. Just be one of the good threads in their hard thing. Day three hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Romans 8:28 is among the most memorized verses in the Bible; many Christians hold onto it in hard seasons, and pastors often explain it carefully so it isn't used to call suffering good.

fork.setup: a friend's child is in the hospital. you want to comfort them with Romans 8:28. what does the verse actually give you?
options: this is good, it happened for a reason.
even this can be woven into good.

fork.reveal: the verse says all things work together for good, not that all things are good. Paul has just spoken of a world groaning in pain.

original.note: Greek: works together, cooperates. the root of our word synergy.

trapdoor: what you thought: everything happens for a reason.
what it means: not that hard things are good, but that God works even hard things together for good for those who love him.
what a scholar hears: several early manuscripts, including one of the oldest papyri, add ho theos, God, as the subject, while other manuscripts leave all things as the subject.

sources.quoted: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

notes: Textual variant in 8:28: 'ho theos' is added in P46, Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus, among others. Confirm the trapdoor wording.
Reformed / Wesleyan / Catholic-Orthodox summary of predestination in 8:29–30 is compressed; confirm fair to each.
The weaver image is the script's own illustration, not from the text; confirm it isn't presented as Paul's.
